explanation.whyCorrect: Mitochondrial acetyl-CoA is condensed with oxaloacetate to citrate, a TCA intermediate that is exported to the cytosol. There citrate lyase cleaves it back to oxaloacetate (which continues the shuttle) and acetyl-CoA, which is used for fatty acid synthesis.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Malate is part of the return arm of the citrate shuttle in the cytosol, not the carrier that exports the acetyl unit.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Malonyl-CoA is formed in the cytosol from acetyl-CoA after the shuttle; it is not the export form.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Oxaloacetate cannot cross the inner mitochondrial membrane directly and is regenerated in the cytosol after citrate is cleaved.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Pyruvate is the return product that re-enters mitochondria; it does not carry the acetyl unit out.

questions.topicName: Lipids and Lipid Metabolism Introduction

questions.stem: During beta-oxidation of an odd-numbered fatty acid, the final three-carbon product propionyl-CoA is converted to succinyl-CoA so it can enter the TCA cycle. This conversion proceeds through a methylmalonyl-CoA intermediate and requires a specific vitamin. Deficiency of which vitamin would impair this step?

explanation.summary: Methylmalonyl-CoA mutase requires cobalamin (B12) to convert propionyl-CoA to succinyl-CoA.
explanation.whyCorrect: Odd-chain fatty acids yield propionyl-CoA, which is converted to succinyl-CoA through a methylmalonyl-CoA intermediate. Methylmalonyl-CoA mutase requires cobalamin, so a B12 deficiency impairs this conversion.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Biotin is the cofactor for carboxylases such as acetyl-CoA carboxylase, not for methylmalonyl-CoA mutase.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Folate participates in one-carbon transfers for nucleotide synthesis, not this mutase reaction.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Pyridoxine supports transamination and other reactions but is not the cofactor for methylmalonyl-CoA mutase.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Vitamin K is required for gamma-carboxylation of clotting factors, unrelated to propionyl-CoA metabolism.

questions.topicName: Lipids and Lipid Metabolism Introduction

questions.stem: A 14-month-old boy presents with poor feeding, muscle weakness, an enlarged and weakened heart (cardiomyopathy), and hypoglycemia. Genetic testing identifies a mutation in SLC22A5 encoding the OCTN2 transporter, impairing cellular carnitine uptake. Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A ketogenic (high-fat) diet to bypass the carnitine defect

explanation.summary: Primary carnitine deficiency from OCTN2 (SLC22A5) mutation is treated with L-carnitine supplementation.
explanation.whyCorrect: Mutations in SLC22A5 impair the OCTN2 transporter that imports carnitine, causing primary carnitine deficiency with encephalopathy, cardiomyopathy, weakness, and hypoglycemia in infancy or early childhood. Depending on the variant, supplementation with L-carnitine can be beneficial by restoring the substrate needed for the carnitine shuttle.

whyWrongByChoice.A: A high-fat diet increases reliance on the impaired fatty acid oxidation pathway and would not correct the carnitine deficit.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Restricting carbohydrate would worsen energy failure, since carbohydrate is the safer fuel when fat oxidation is impaired.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Biotin addresses carboxylase reactions and would not replace deficient carnitine.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Cobalamin is needed for methylmalonyl-CoA mutase, not for carnitine transport.

questions.topicName: Lipids and Lipid Metabolism Introduction

questions.stem: A 55-year-old man with chronic pancreatitis has ongoing fat malabsorption producing bulky, greasy, foul-smelling stools (steatorrhea). Given that lipoproteins carry certain vitamins in their hydrophobic core, deficiency of which group of vitamins is the major concern in this patient?

explanation.summary: Fat malabsorption and steatorrhea threaten the fat-soluble vitamins A, D, E, and K.
explanation.whyCorrect: Dietary fat malabsorption produces steatorrhea, and because the fat-soluble vitamins A, D, E, and K are absorbed and carried within lipoproteins along with dietary lipid, their depletion is the major concern when fat absorption fails.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Folate and cobalamin are water-soluble vitamins not carried in the hydrophobic lipoprotein core.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Niacin and thiamine are water-soluble B vitamins unaffected by fat malabsorption in this way.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Vitamin C is water-soluble and absorbed independently of dietary fat.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The B vitamins are water-soluble and are not lost preferentially with dietary fat.

questions.topicName: Lipids and Lipid Metabolism Introduction

questions.stem: A biochemist incubates isolated liver mitochondria with fatty acids of different chain lengths and measures the rate of beta-oxidation with and without added carnitine. Which of the following fatty acids would show oxidation only when carnitine is present?

explanation.summary: Only long-chain fatty acids (13 or more carbons) require the carnitine shuttle to enter the mitochondrial matrix.
explanation.whyCorrect: Fatty acids are classified by chain length as short chain (5 or fewer carbons), medium chain (6-12 carbons), and long chain (13 or more carbons). SCFAs and MCFAs readily diffuse into the mitochondrial matrix, but LCFAs require modification and transport across the inner mitochondrial membrane via the carnitine shuttle. A 16-carbon fatty acid such as palmitate is therefore the only listed substrate whose oxidation depends on carnitine.

whyWrongByChoice.A: A 4-carbon fatty acid is a short-chain fatty acid that diffuses directly into the matrix without carnitine.
whyWrongByChoice.B: An 8-carbon fatty acid is a medium-chain fatty acid and does not need the carnitine shuttle.
whyWrongByChoice.C: A 10-carbon fatty acid falls within the 6-12 carbon medium-chain range and diffuses into the matrix freely.
whyWrongByChoice.D: A 12-carbon fatty acid is at the upper limit of the medium-chain class and still enters the matrix without carnitine.

questions.topicName: Lipids and Lipid Metabolism Introduction

questions.stem: A first-year student is asked to compare the structure of a plasma lipoprotein particle with that of a cell membrane. Which of the following best describes the organization of a lipoprotein transport complex?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A phospholipid bilayer surrounding a hydrophobic core

choices.label: B
choices.text: A phospholipid bilayer surrounding an aqueous core

choices.label: C
choices.text: A protein shell without any phospholipid layer

choices.label: D
choices.text: A single phospholipid layer surrounding a hydrophobic core

choices.label: E
choices.text: A single phospholipid layer surrounding an aqueous core

explanation.summary: Lipoproteins have a single phospholipid layer, not a bilayer, around a hydrophobic core.
explanation.whyCorrect: Lipoprotein macromolecular transport complexes have a single phospholipid layer (not a bilayer like cell membranes) and a hydrophobic core. The hydrophilic exterior allows travel through the blood, while the hydrophobic interior carries lipids such as TGs and cholesterol along with fat-soluble vitamins.

whyWrongByChoice.A: A bilayer is the organization of a cell membrane, not a lipoprotein particle.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Lipoproteins have neither a bilayer nor an aqueous core; the interior is hydrophobic to carry lipids.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Lipoproteins do carry apolipoproteins, but their surface is built from a single phospholipid layer rather than a pure protein shell.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The single phospholipid layer is correct, but the core is hydrophobic, not aqueous, because its purpose is to carry water-insoluble lipids.

questions.topicName: Lipids and Lipid Metabolism Introduction

questions.stem: A 47-year-old woman presents with severe epigastric pain radiating to the back. Serum pancreatic lipase and alpha-amylase are markedly elevated, consistent with pancreatic dysfunction. In healthy digestion, the lipase that is elevated in this patient normally generates which of the following products within the small intestine?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Cholesteryl esters and free fatty acids

choices.label: B
choices.text: Fatty acyl-carnitine and free coenzyme A

choices.label: C
choices.text: Free glycerol and three long-chain fatty acids

choices.label: E
choices.text: Short- and medium-chain fatty acids absorbed into blood

explanation.summary: Pancreatic lipase hydrolyzes dietary TGs to free LCFAs plus a 2-monoacylglycerol.
explanation.whyCorrect: Pancreatic lipase produces a mix of free LCFAs and a 2-monoacylglycerol (glycerol with a single fatty acid attached to the middle carbon) within the small intestine, and it has the major role in dietary TG digestion. Its circulating level is used along with pancreatic alpha-amylase as a biomarker for pancreatic dysfunction.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Cholesteryl esters are formed by ACAT within enterocytes, not by pancreatic lipase.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Fatty acyl-carnitine is produced by carnitine acyltransferase-1 during mitochondrial import, unrelated to digestion.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Pancreatic lipase does not strip all three fatty acids to free glycerol; it leaves a fatty acid on the middle carbon as 2-monoacylglycerol.
whyWrongByChoice.E: SCFAs and MCFAs are released mainly by lingual and gastric lipase acting on milk fats, not by pancreatic lipase in the intestine.

questions.topicName: Lipids and Lipid Metabolism Introduction

questions.stem: A breastfed 2-week-old infant digests milk fat beginning in the mouth and stomach. The short- and medium-chain fatty acids released by lingual and gastric lipase are handled in which of the following ways?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Esterified to cholesterol by ACAT within enterocytes

choices.label: C
choices.text: Held in the lumen until hydrolysis by pancreatic lipase

choices.label: D
choices.text: Loaded onto VLDL by microsomal transfer protein

choices.label: E
choices.text: Repackaged into TGs in enterocytes and secreted in chylomicrons

explanation.summary: SCFAs and MCFAs released by lingual and gastric lipase are absorbed directly into the bloodstream.
explanation.whyCorrect: Lingual and gastric lipase partially digest and emulsify fats within the mouth and stomach, typically releasing SCFAs and MCFAs, which are common in milk. These smaller fats are directly absorbed into the bloodstream, and these enzymes play only a minor role in overall dietary TG digestion.

whyWrongByChoice.B: ACAT esterifies dietary cholesterol, not short- and medium-chain fatty acids.
whyWrongByChoice.C: SCFAs and MCFAs are already freed by lingual and gastric lipase and do not wait for pancreatic lipase.
whyWrongByChoice.D: VLDL carries lipids synthesized by the liver; absorbed milk fatty acids are not loaded onto VLDL in the gut.
whyWrongByChoice.E: It is the LCFAs released by pancreatic lipase that are repackaged into TGs in enterocytes and released in chylomicrons.

questions.topicName: Lipids and Lipid Metabolism Introduction

questions.stem: A 2-year-old boy with medium-chain acyl-CoA dehydrogenase deficiency is admitted with vomiting and lethargy after a febrile illness. Serum glucose is 38 mg/dL and urine ketones are absent. Which of the following best explains the absence of ketones despite hypoglycemia?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Carnitine cannot be imported into cells to form acyl-carnitines

choices.label: B
choices.text: Elevated malonyl-CoA is preventing fatty acid entry into mitochondria

choices.label: C
choices.text: Excess insulin secretion is suppressing ketogenesis

choices.label: D
choices.text: Ketone bodies are being consumed as substrate for gluconeogenesis

choices.label: E
choices.text: Ketone body production requires fatty acid catabolism, which is blocked

explanation.summary: MCAD deficiency causes hypoketotic hypoglycemia because ketone body production requires fatty acid catabolism.
explanation.whyCorrect: MCAD deficiency is the most common disorder of fatty acid oxidation. It results in hypoketotic hypoglycemia because ketone body production requires fatty acid catabolism, and fatty acid oxidation is required to produce the ATP that fuels gluconeogenesis during fasting. Fatty acyl carnitines accumulate in the blood, and patients present acutely with hyperammonemia and hypoglycemia after prolonged fasting or infection.

whyWrongByChoice.A: This child can form acyl-carnitines (they accumulate in blood); impaired carnitine import describes primary carnitine deficiency, not MCAD deficiency.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Malonyl-CoA rises in the fed state; during fasting stress the block is at the medium-chain dehydrogenase, not at CPT1.
whyWrongByChoice.C: This child is hypoglycemic during a fasting stress; insulin excess is not the mechanism of the missing ketones.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Ketone bodies are not a substrate for gluconeogenesis; the problem is that they cannot be made.

questions.topicName: Lipids and Lipid Metabolism Introduction

questions.stem: Cholesterol is an essential precursor for bile salts and steroid hormones, and roughly 20% of it is obtained from the diet. Two different enzymes esterify cholesterol so it can be packed and transported. Which of the following correctly pairs each enzyme with the site where it acts?

choices.label: A
choices.text: ACAT: capillary endothelium; LCAT: intracellular endoplasmic reticulum

choices.label: B
choices.text: ACAT: circulating HDL; LCAT: enterocyte endoplasmic reticulum

choices.label: C
choices.text: ACAT: circulating VLDL; LCAT: capillary endothelium

choices.label: D
choices.text: ACAT: hepatocyte lysosome; LCAT: enterocyte endoplasmic reticulum

choices.label: E
choices.text: ACAT: intracellular endoplasmic reticulum; LCAT: circulating HDL

explanation.summary: ACAT esterifies cholesterol intracellularly in the ER; LCAT esterifies circulating cholesterol on HDL.
explanation.whyCorrect: Dietary cholesterol is converted into cholesteryl esters by acyl-CoA cholesterol acyltransferase (ACAT) within intestinal enterocytes, and ACAT functions intracellularly within the ER. In contrast, LCAT, activated by apoA-I on HDL, acts on circulating (endogenous) cholesterol. Cholesteryl esters structurally allow tight packing and increase the amount of cholesterol carried within lipoproteins.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Capillary endothelium is where lipoprotein lipase acts on TGs; neither cholesterol esterase works there, and LCAT is not intracellular.
whyWrongByChoice.B: This reverses the two enzymes: LCAT is the one that works on circulating HDL cholesterol, and ACAT is the intracellular ER enzyme.
whyWrongByChoice.C: ACAT is not a circulating enzyme on VLDL, and LCAT acts on HDL cholesterol in plasma rather than on the capillary wall.
whyWrongByChoice.D: ACAT is an ER enzyme, not a lysosomal one, and LCAT works in the circulation, not in the enterocyte ER.

questions.topicName: Lipids and Lipid Metabolism Introduction

questions.stem: A researcher isolates plasma lipoproteins and probes each fraction with antibodies to individual apolipoproteins. One apolipoprotein is synthesized only by the liver and is detected on VLDL and LDL but is absent from chylomicrons and HDL. Which apolipoprotein is this?

explanation.summary: apoB-100 is the liver-derived structural protein found only on VLDL and LDL.
explanation.whyCorrect: apoB-100 originates in the liver, associates with VLDL and LDL, and serves as a structural protein that contains the LDL-receptor binding domain. It is not found on chylomicrons (which use apoB-48 from the intestine) or on HDL, which is the only plasma lipoprotein that lacks apoB.

whyWrongByChoice.A: apoA-I originates in both the liver and intestine and is found on HDL and chylomicrons.
whyWrongByChoice.C: apoB-48 is made by the intestine and is the structural protein of chylomicrons, not VLDL or LDL.
whyWrongByChoice.D: apoC-II is liver-derived but is found on HDL, VLDL, and chylomicrons, not restricted to VLDL and LDL.
whyWrongByChoice.E: apoE is liver-derived but is found on HDL, VLDL, and chylomicrons.

questions.topicName: Lipids and Lipid Metabolism Introduction

questions.stem: Three hours after a fatty meal, chylomicrons in a healthy adult have had most of their triglyceride removed by lipoprotein lipase in adipose and muscle capillaries. The resulting chylomicron remnants are cleared from the circulation by the liver. Which apolipoprotein mediates this hepatic uptake?

explanation.summary: apoE mediates uptake of chylomicron remnants (and to a smaller extent IDL) by the liver.
explanation.whyCorrect: apoE, supplied from the HDL reservoir, mediates uptake of chylomicron remnants and, to a smaller extent, IDL remnants by the liver. Chylomicrons are present in circulation for 2-3 hours after a meal, and after LPL hydrolyzes their TG content the apoE-bearing remnants are taken up by hepatic receptors that recognize apoE.

whyWrongByChoice.A: apoA-I activates LCAT on HDL and has no role in remnant uptake.
whyWrongByChoice.B: apoB-100 is found on VLDL and LDL, not chylomicrons, and is the ligand for LDL-receptor uptake of LDL.
whyWrongByChoice.C: apoB-48 is the structural protein of chylomicrons required for their assembly, but LDL receptors do not bind apoB-48 and it does not mediate remnant uptake.
whyWrongByChoice.D: apoC-II activates extrahepatic lipoprotein lipase; it is involved in TG removal, not hepatic remnant clearance.

questions.topicName: Lipids and Lipid Metabolism Introduction

questions.stem: A pharmacologist studies an experimental drug that completely blocks cholesteryl ester transfer protein (CETP) in plasma. Which of the following changes in HDL cholesteryl ester content and LCAT activity is the most likely direct consequence?

choices.label: A
choices.text: HDL cholesteryl ester accumulates; LCAT becomes product-inhibited

choices.label: B
choices.text: HDL cholesteryl ester decreases; LCAT is activated by apoC-II

choices.label: C
choices.text: HDL cholesteryl ester decreases; LCAT product inhibition is relieved

choices.label: D
choices.text: HDL cholesteryl ester is unchanged; LCAT is inhibited by apoA-I

choices.label: E
choices.text: HDL triglyceride increases; LCAT activity is unchanged

explanation.summary: CETP removes cholesteryl ester from HDL, relieving product inhibition of LCAT; blocking it lets CE build up and inhibit LCAT.
explanation.whyCorrect: Once LPL shrinks VLDL in the circulation, CETP catalyzes a swap of TAGs within VLDL for cholesteryl ester within HDL. This exchange relieves product inhibition of LCAT, allowing continued cholesterol esterification. If CETP is blocked, cholesteryl ester is no longer exported from HDL, so it accumulates and LCAT becomes product-inhibited.

whyWrongByChoice.B: apoC-II activates lipoprotein lipase, not LCAT, and HDL cholesteryl ester would increase, not decrease.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Without CETP, cholesteryl ester cannot leave HDL, so it rises rather than falls, and product inhibition of LCAT worsens rather than being relieved.
whyWrongByChoice.D: apoA-I activates LCAT rather than inhibiting it, and HDL cholesteryl ester would clearly change.
whyWrongByChoice.E: CETP delivers TAG to HDL in exchange for CE; blocking it reduces, not increases, HDL TAG, and LCAT is affected through product inhibition.

questions.topicName: Lipids and Lipid Metabolism Introduction

questions.stem: A patient asks why an expensive expanded lipid panel that reports VLDL and IDL is unnecessary. The physician explains that VLDL is mainly triglyceride, and as the triglyceride is removed VLDL becomes IDL and eventually LDL, which is already on the standard panel. Working with CETP, which enzyme further enriches the cholesterol content of the particle as it is converted to LDL?

explanation.summary: CETP promotes LDL formation from VLDL with help from hepatic lipase, which further enriches cholesterol content.
explanation.whyCorrect: After LPL reduces VLDL size, CETP swaps VLDL TAGs for HDL cholesteryl esters. CETP promotes LDL formation from VLDL via help from hepatic lipase, which further enriches the cholesterol content, and ultimately the exchanged cholesteryl esters are taken up by the liver in an LDL particle formed from VLDL. Because triglyceride and LDL levels already reflect this pathway, the extra VLDL and IDL measurements add little.

whyWrongByChoice.A: ACAT esterifies dietary cholesterol inside enterocytes and is not involved in plasma lipoprotein remodeling.
whyWrongByChoice.C: LCAT esterifies cholesterol on HDL; it does not act on the VLDL-to-LDL conversion.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Lipoprotein lipase performs the initial TG hydrolysis that shrinks VLDL in peripheral capillaries but is not the enzyme partnered with CETP for the final cholesterol enrichment.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Pancreatic lipase digests dietary TGs in the intestinal lumen, not circulating lipoproteins.

questions.topicName: Lipids and Lipid Metabolism Introduction

questions.stem: An antibody directed against the shared region of apoB-48 and apoB-100 is used to precipitate lipoproteins from human plasma. Which of the following lipoproteins would remain in the supernatant?

explanation.summary: HDL is the only plasma lipoprotein that lacks apoB.
explanation.whyCorrect: HDL is the only plasma lipoprotein that lacks apoB (apoB-48 or apoB-100). It serves as a circulating reservoir of apoC-II and apoE and is critical in reverse cholesterol transport. All other listed lipoproteins carry an apoB and would be precipitated by the antibody.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Chylomicrons carry apoB-48 as their structural protein and would be precipitated.
whyWrongByChoice.C: IDL is formed from VLDL and retains apoB-100, so it would be precipitated.
whyWrongByChoice.D: LDL contains only one apoprotein, apoB-100, and would be precipitated.
whyWrongByChoice.E: VLDL carries apoB-100 and would be precipitated.

questions.topicName: Lipids and Lipid Metabolism Introduction

questions.stem: Plasma lipoproteins are separated by ultracentrifugation and each fraction is analyzed for its relative triglyceride and cholesterol content. Which fraction has the highest cholesterol content with low triglyceride?

explanation.summary: LDL has the highest cholesterol (cholesteryl ester) content and low triglyceride.
explanation.whyCorrect: Lipoproteins are distinguished by density, which is determined by their relative cholesterol, TG, and protein content. LDL particles have low TAG and the highest cholesterol content, reflecting their role in delivering hepatic cholesterol to peripheral tissues. Chylomicrons have the highest TAG and lowest cholesterol, VLDL has high TAG and low cholesterol, and HDL has the lowest TAG with high (but not the highest) cholesterol.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Chylomicrons have the highest TAG and the lowest cholesterol content of all lipoproteins.
whyWrongByChoice.B: HDL has the lowest TAG content and high cholesterol, but LDL is the fraction with the highest cholesterol content.
whyWrongByChoice.C: IDL is an intermediate formed as VLDL loses TG; it is not the cholesterol-richest fraction.
whyWrongByChoice.E: VLDL is TAG-rich with low cholesterol, delivering hepatic triglycerides to peripheral tissues.

questions.topicName: Lipids and Lipid Metabolism Introduction

questions.stem: A healthy 30-year-old man has blood drawn 2 hours after eating a large fatty meal, and the plasma appears milky. A second sample drawn after an overnight fast is clear. Which of the following best explains the milky appearance of the first sample?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Chylomicrons, because of their large size and high triglyceride content

choices.label: B
choices.text: HDL particles, because of their high protein and phospholipid content

choices.label: C
choices.text: IDL particles, because of their retained apoE content

choices.label: D
choices.text: LDL particles, because of their high cholesteryl ester content

choices.label: E
choices.text: VLDL particles, because of their large size and high triglyceride content

explanation.summary: Chylomicrons, present 2-3 hours after a meal, make plasma milky because of their large size and high TG content.
explanation.whyCorrect: Chylomicrons are present in circulation after a meal for 2-3 hours and emerge from the small intestine. They are the physically largest and most TG-enriched lipoprotein particle, and when enriched in circulation they cause blood plasma to have a milky appearance due to their large size and high TG content. After an overnight fast they have been cleared and the plasma is clear.

whyWrongByChoice.B: HDL is the smallest lipoprotein and does not produce a milky appearance.
whyWrongByChoice.C: IDL is a transient VLDL-derived intermediate and does not account for postprandial lipemia.
whyWrongByChoice.D: LDL is small and cholesterol-rich; it does not cloud plasma and is not a postprandial particle.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Although VLDL is also TG-enriched, VLDL particles are smaller and will not give a milky appearance to the plasma.

questions.topicName: Lipids and Lipid Metabolism Introduction

questions.stem: A molecular biologist expresses the LDL receptor in cultured cells that normally lack it and then tests which lipoprotein particles are internalized by receptor-mediated endocytosis. Binding is expected for particles carrying which of the following apolipoproteins?

explanation.summary: LDL receptors bind apoB-100 (but not apoB-48) and also recognize apoE.
explanation.whyCorrect: Tissue uptake of LDL particles is accomplished as LDL receptors bind apoB-100 (but not B-48) for receptor-mediated endocytosis. These same receptors also recognize and bind apoE, which is why IDL and chylomicron remnants bearing apoE can be taken up by the liver.

whyWrongByChoice.A: apoA-I activates LCAT and apoC-II activates lipoprotein lipase; neither is a ligand for the LDL receptor.
whyWrongByChoice.B: apoB-100 is correct, but apoC-II is an enzyme activator rather than a receptor ligand.
whyWrongByChoice.D: apoB-48 is explicitly not bound by the LDL receptor, so chylomicrons themselves are not internalized this way.
whyWrongByChoice.E: apoE is a ligand, but apoB-48 is not recognized by the LDL receptor.

questions.topicName: Lipids and Lipid Metabolism Introduction

questions.stem: A 62-year-old man with long-standing elevated LDL cholesterol dies of a myocardial infarction. Autopsy of his coronary arteries shows atherosclerotic plaques containing numerous lipid-laden inflammatory macrophages. Which of the following processes most directly hastens the formation of these cells?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Esterification of macrophage cholesterol by LCAT

choices.label: B
choices.text: Exchange of cholesteryl ester for triglyceride by CETP

choices.label: C
choices.text: Hydrolysis of VLDL triglyceride by lipoprotein lipase

choices.label: D
choices.text: Uptake of HDL by macrophages through apoA-I

choices.label: E
choices.text: Uptake of oxidized LDL through macrophage scavenger receptors

explanation.summary: Oxidized LDL taken up by scavenger receptors on macrophages accelerates foam cell formation.
explanation.whyCorrect: The adverse health risk of LDL is attributed to the fact that macrophages express LDL receptors and can be filled with cholesterol to become inflammatory foam cells. This process is hastened by oxidized LDL molecules, which are taken up by scavenger receptors on macrophages. Foam cells promote the atherosclerotic plaques associated with cardiovascular disease.

whyWrongByChoice.A: LCAT esterifies cholesterol on circulating HDL, not within macrophages, and supports reverse cholesterol transport rather than plaque formation.
whyWrongByChoice.B: CETP exchanges lipids between VLDL and HDL in plasma; it does not fill macrophages with cholesterol.
whyWrongByChoice.C: LPL hydrolysis of TG delivers fatty acids to adipose and muscle and is not the mechanism of foam cell formation.
whyWrongByChoice.D: HDL removes cholesterol from peripheral tissues in reverse cholesterol transport; it does not load macrophages with lipid.

questions.topicName: Lipids and Lipid Metabolism Introduction

questions.stem: A 44-year-old woman with a strong family history of early heart disease has a normal standard lipid panel. A specialized test reports an elevated level of lipoprotein little a, Lp(a). Which of the following is the most accurate statement about this result?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Lp(a) is a chylomicron remnant measured on every routine panel

choices.label: B
choices.text: Lp(a) is a modified HDL that marks reduced cardiovascular risk

choices.label: C
choices.text: Lp(a) is a modified LDL that marks increased cardiovascular risk

choices.label: D
choices.text: Lp(a) is a modified VLDL that is lowered by dietary fat restriction

choices.label: E
choices.text: Lp(a) is an IDL variant with an established lowering therapy

explanation.summary: Lp(a) is a modified LDL containing apolipoprotein a; elevated levels are a marker of cardiovascular risk.
explanation.whyCorrect: Lipoprotein little a is a modified form of LDL particles that contains a large glycoprotein called apolipoprotein a. Elevated levels of Lp(a) have been associated with increased risk of cardiovascular disease. It is not yet a routinely measured lipoprotein and there is no intervention for lowering high levels, but it is often used as a marker of cardiovascular risk.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Lp(a) is not a chylomicron remnant and is not yet routinely measured.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Lp(a) is derived from LDL, not HDL, and elevated levels increase rather than reduce risk.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Lp(a) is a modified LDL, not VLDL, and there is no established intervention for lowering it.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Lp(a) is not an IDL variant, and no intervention for lowering high levels currently exists.

questions.topicName: Lipids and Lipid Metabolism Introduction

questions.stem: A hepatocyte simultaneously contains the machinery for building fatty acids and for breaking them down, yet the two processes do not compete within the same compartment. Which of the following correctly identifies the subcellular location of fatty acid synthesis and of beta-oxidation, respectively?

explanation.summary: Fatty acid synthesis is cytoplasmic; beta-oxidation occurs in the mitochondrial matrix.
explanation.whyCorrect: Fatty acid synthesis occurs primarily in the liver and is localized to the cytoplasm, while fatty acid oxidation occurs within the mitochondrial matrix. This compartmentalization ensures that the processes do not compete, that is, simultaneous production and destruction within the same cell.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Beta-oxidation does not occur in the cytoplasm; it takes place in the mitochondrial matrix.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The ER is the site of ACAT cholesterol esterification, and peroxisomes handle only the initial oxidation of very-long-chain fatty acids.
whyWrongByChoice.D: This reverses the compartments; synthesis is cytoplasmic and oxidation is mitochondrial.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Fatty acid synthesis is not mitochondrial; the growing chain is attached to fatty acid synthase in the cytosol.

questions.topicName: Lipids and Lipid Metabolism Introduction

questions.stem: After a large carbohydrate-rich meal, a healthy adult has a rise in serum insulin, and hepatic fatty acid synthesis increases. Which of the following best describes the covalent mechanism by which insulin increases the activity of acetyl-CoA carboxylase?

choices.label: C
choices.text: Decreased transcription of the acetyl-CoA carboxylase gene

explanation.summary: Insulin promotes dephosphorylation of acetyl-CoA carboxylase, activating this anabolic enzyme.
explanation.whyCorrect: Acetyl-CoA carboxylase is an anabolic enzyme whose activity is favored when energy sources are abundant and insulin is high. Insulin ultimately promotes dephosphorylation of this enzyme via a phosphatase to promote activity. Insulin also favors glycolysis to generate citrate, which allosterically activates the enzyme.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Malonyl-CoA is the product of the enzyme and inhibits CPT1; the allosteric activator is citrate.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Palmitoyl-CoA is the product-derived negative feedback inhibitor, not a mechanism of insulin activation.
whyWrongByChoice.C: A high-calorie diet increases, not decreases, transcription of the acetyl-CoA carboxylase gene; a low-calorie diet reduces it.
whyWrongByChoice.E: AMP-activated protein kinase phosphorylates and inactivates acetyl-CoA carboxylase during low-energy states, the opposite of insulin's effect.

questions.topicName: Lipids and Lipid Metabolism Introduction

questions.stem: A marathon runner in the final miles of a race has depleted hepatic glycogen, and cellular AMP is accumulating in liver and muscle. Which of the following sequences of changes in acetyl-CoA carboxylase (ACC) activity, malonyl-CoA level, and carnitine acyltransferase-1 (CPT1) activity is expected?

choices.label: A
choices.text: ACC activated; malonyl-CoA falls; CPT1 disinhibited

choices.label: B
choices.text: ACC activated; malonyl-CoA rises; CPT1 inhibited

choices.label: C
choices.text: ACC inactivated; malonyl-CoA falls; CPT1 disinhibited

choices.label: D
choices.text: ACC inactivated; malonyl-CoA rises; CPT1 inhibited

choices.label: E
choices.text: ACC unchanged; malonyl-CoA falls; CPT1 inhibited

explanation.summary: Low energy activates AMPK, which phosphorylates and inactivates ACC, lowering malonyl-CoA and freeing CPT1 for fatty acid oxidation.
explanation.whyCorrect: Low energy levels (AMP accumulating) activate AMP-activated protein kinase, which phosphorylates and inactivates acetyl-CoA carboxylase. With ACC inactive, malonyl-CoA production falls. Because malonyl-CoA is the allosteric inhibitor of carnitine acyltransferase-1, its decline relieves CPT1 inhibition, allowing long-chain fatty acids to enter the mitochondria for beta-oxidation and ketone body synthesis.

whyWrongByChoice.A: An activated ACC would raise malonyl-CoA, not lower it, and AMPK inactivates rather than activates ACC.
whyWrongByChoice.B: This describes the fed state driven by insulin and citrate, not the low-energy state signaled by AMP.
whyWrongByChoice.D: If ACC is inactivated, malonyl-CoA cannot rise; the product of an inactive enzyme falls.
whyWrongByChoice.E: ACC is not unchanged during AMP accumulation, and a fall in malonyl-CoA would relieve rather than maintain CPT1 inhibition.

questions.topicName: Lipids and Lipid Metabolism Introduction

questions.stem: In a hepatocyte actively synthesizing fatty acids, the final 16-carbon product is converted to its coenzyme A derivative. Which of the following molecules provides negative feedback inhibition on acetyl-CoA carboxylase?

explanation.summary: Palmitoyl-CoA, the CoA derivative of the end product palmitate, feeds back to inhibit acetyl-CoA carboxylase.
explanation.whyCorrect: The ultimate product of fatty acid synthesis, palmitate, is converted to its coenzyme A derivative, palmitoyl-CoA, which inhibits acetyl-CoA carboxylase. This negative feedback prevents continued malonyl-CoA production once the end product has accumulated.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Acetyl-CoA is the substrate of the carboxylase, and its abundance favors enzyme activity.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Citrate allosterically activates acetyl-CoA carboxylase rather than inhibiting it.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Insulin promotes dephosphorylation and activation of the enzyme.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Malonyl-CoA is the product of acetyl-CoA carboxylase and inhibits CPT1, not the carboxylase itself.

questions.topicName: Lipids and Lipid Metabolism Introduction

questions.stem: Fatty acid synthase elongates the growing chain by repeated cycles of condensation, reduction, dehydration, and reduction. Each of the two reduction steps consumes one molecule of NADPH. Which of the following pairs of pathways supplies this NADPH?

choices.label: D
choices.text: Pentose phosphate pathway and malic enzyme

choices.label: E
choices.text: TCA cycle and the electron transport chain

explanation.summary: NADPH for fatty acid synthesis comes from the pentose phosphate pathway and malic enzyme of the citrate shuttle.
explanation.whyCorrect: Fatty acid synthase catalyzes a repetitive four-step sequence in which the chain is elongated by two-carbon units provided by the 3-carbon malonyl-CoA. Each reduction uses one molecule of NADPH supplied by the pentose phosphate pathway or the malic enzyme from the citrate shuttle, in which cytosolic malate is converted to pyruvate with generation of NADPH.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Beta-oxidation and ketogenesis are catabolic pathways that do not supply reducing equivalents for synthesis.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Citrate lyase releases acetyl-CoA and oxaloacetate in the cytosol and citrate synthase forms citrate in the matrix; neither generates NADPH.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Glycolysis and PDH provide pyruvate and acetyl-CoA carbon, generating NADH rather than NADPH.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The TCA cycle and electron transport chain produce NADH and ATP, not the NADPH used by fatty acid synthase.

questions.topicName: Lipids and Lipid Metabolism Introduction

questions.stem: A researcher purifies fatty acid synthase from liver cytosol and supplies it with acetyl-CoA, malonyl-CoA, and NADPH. Which of the following is the primary fatty acid released by this enzyme complex?

explanation.summary: The primary product of fatty acid synthase is palmitic acid, a 16-carbon fatty acid.
explanation.whyCorrect: The primary product of fatty acid synthesis is palmitic acid, a 16-carbon fatty acid. After activation to a CoA derivative, palmitate is the substrate that is elongated to generate a series of other fatty acids that are packaged into TGs for delivery in VLDL.

whyWrongByChoice.A: A 12-carbon chain is a medium-chain fatty acid and is not the released product of the synthase.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Longer fatty acids such as 18-carbon chains are generated by subsequent elongation of palmitoyl-CoA, not directly by fatty acid synthase.
whyWrongByChoice.D: A 20-carbon chain requires elongation steps beyond fatty acid synthase.
whyWrongByChoice.E: A 22-carbon chain is a very-long-chain fatty acid produced by elongation, not the synthase product.

questions.topicName: Lipids and Lipid Metabolism Introduction

questions.stem: A long-chain fatty acyl-CoA in the cytosol must be delivered to the mitochondrial matrix for beta-oxidation. Which of the following steps of this transport process takes place within the mitochondrial matrix?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A translocase exchanges fatty acyl-carnitine for free carnitine

choices.label: B
choices.text: Carnitine acyltransferase-1 converts fatty acyl-CoA to fatty acyl-carnitine

choices.label: C
choices.text: Carnitine acyltransferase-2 converts fatty acyl-carnitine back to fatty acyl-CoA

choices.label: D
choices.text: Fatty acyl-carnitine diffuses across the outer mitochondrial membrane

explanation.summary: Carnitine acyltransferase-2 regenerates fatty acyl-CoA from fatty acyl-carnitine once inside the matrix.
explanation.whyCorrect: Carnitine acyltransferase-1 converts fatty acyl-CoA to fatty acyl-carnitine, which readily diffuses across the outer but not the inner mitochondrial membrane. An antiporter in the inner membrane, carnitine-acylcarnitine translocase, exchanges cytoplasmic fatty acyl-carnitine for mitochondrial free carnitine. Once within the matrix, carnitine acyltransferase-2 converts fatty acyl-carnitine back to fatty acyl-CoA, which is catabolized by beta-oxidation. Carnitine acyltransferases are also called carnitine palmitoyltransferases (CPTs).

whyWrongByChoice.A: The translocase is an antiporter within the inner membrane; it moves the acyl-carnitine across rather than acting within the matrix.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Carnitine acyltransferase-1 acts on the cytosolic side of the outer membrane, before the fatty acid reaches the matrix.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Diffusion across the outer membrane delivers fatty acyl-carnitine to the intermembrane space, not the matrix.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Malonyl-CoA inhibition of CPT1 occurs at the outer membrane in the cytosol, not in the matrix.

questions.topicName: Lipids and Lipid Metabolism Introduction

questions.stem: A biochemist follows the catabolism of a 26-carbon saturated fatty acid in a hepatocyte. Where does the initial round of beta-oxidation of this fatty acid occur, and why?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Cytoplasm, because fatty acid synthase can run in reverse

choices.label: B
choices.text: Endoplasmic reticulum, because ACAT esterifies the chain first

choices.label: C
choices.text: Mitochondrial matrix, because LCAD acts on chains over 22 carbons

choices.label: D
choices.text: Mitochondrial matrix, because MCAD acts on all chain lengths

choices.label: E
choices.text: Peroxisome, because only it has a dehydrogenase for these chains

explanation.summary: Very-long-chain fatty acids (22 or more carbons) begin beta-oxidation in peroxisomes, which uniquely contain the required acyl-CoA dehydrogenase.
explanation.whyCorrect: Very-long-chain fatty acids containing 22 or more carbons undergo initial beta-oxidation in peroxisomes, and after chain shortening they are further catabolized by beta-oxidation in the mitochondria. This is because peroxisomes but not mitochondria contain fatty acyl-CoA dehydrogenase enzymes that act on VLCFAs.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Fatty acid synthase is an anabolic cytosolic enzyme and does not carry out beta-oxidation.
whyWrongByChoice.B: ACAT esterifies cholesterol in the ER and has no role in fatty acid degradation.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Mitochondrial LCAD handles long-chain fatty acids but mitochondria lack the dehydrogenases that act on chains of 22 or more carbons.
whyWrongByChoice.D: MCAD acts on medium-chain fatty acids of 6-12 carbons, not on very-long-chain substrates.

questions.topicName: Lipids and Lipid Metabolism Introduction

questions.stem: A researcher studies the endogenous pathway that converts acetyl-CoA into cholesterol in hepatocytes. She wishes to target the single step that is rate-limiting and is exploited by a major class of lipid-lowering drugs. Which enzyme should she target?

explanation.summary: HMG-CoA reductase catalyzes the rate-limiting step of cholesterol synthesis and is the target of statins.
explanation.whyCorrect: HMG-CoA reductase reduces HMG-CoA to mevalonate using NADPH and is the rate-limiting, most clinically salient step of cytoplasmic cholesterol synthesis. Statins competitively inhibit this enzyme to lower hepatic cholesterol production.

whyWrongByChoice.A: HMG-CoA lyase cleaves HMG-CoA to acetoacetate in ketone body synthesis, not cholesterol synthesis.
whyWrongByChoice.C: HMG-CoA synthase forms HMG-CoA but does not catalyze the rate-limiting reduction and is central to ketogenesis in the mitochondrial matrix.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Squalene is a downstream precursor of cholesterol; its formation is not the rate-limiting, statin-targeted step.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Thiolase condenses two acetyl-CoA into acetoacetyl-CoA and is not the rate-limiting or drug-targeted step.

questions.topicName: Lipids and Lipid Metabolism: Cholesterol Synthesis and Ketone Bodies

questions.stem: A 58-year-old man is started on a statin for hypercholesterolemia. Several weeks later his plasma LDL is markedly reduced. Which of the following mechanisms best explains the fall in plasma LDL?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Decreased intestinal absorption of dietary cholesterol

choices.label: B
choices.text: Direct binding and clearance of LDL particles by the drug

choices.label: C
choices.text: Enhanced biliary excretion of free cholesterol

choices.label: E
choices.text: Inhibition of lipoprotein lipase in capillaries

explanation.summary: By lowering hepatic cholesterol synthesis, statins drive the liver to upregulate LDL receptors, which clears LDL from plasma.
explanation.whyCorrect: When statins inhibit HMG-CoA reductase, hepatic cholesterol production drops while the liver still needs cholesterol for processes like bile salt synthesis. Hepatocytes compensate by increasing LDL receptor expression on their surface to take up cholesterol from the circulation, and this increased receptor expression is what lowers plasma LDL.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Statins act on hepatic synthesis, not on intestinal cholesterol absorption.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Statins do not physically bind or clear LDL particles; they act on an intracellular enzyme.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The brick attributes LDL lowering to hepatic LDL receptor upregulation, not to increased biliary cholesterol excretion.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Lipoprotein lipase hydrolyzes triglycerides in lipoproteins and is not the mechanism of statin-induced LDL lowering.

questions.topicName: Lipids and Lipid Metabolism: Cholesterol Synthesis and Ketone Bodies

questions.stem: A 62-year-old woman taking a statin develops diffuse muscle aches without weakness. Research on statin-associated myalgia points to a deficiency of a specific molecule in muscle tissue. Which molecule is most likely reduced?

explanation.summary: Statin-related muscle pain is linked to suboptimal coenzyme Q (ubiquinone) in muscle.
explanation.whyCorrect: Research shows patients on statins with muscle aches have suboptimal levels of coenzyme Q (ubiquinone), a component of the electron transport chain that shares the mevalonate pathway with cholesterol. Many patients therefore take CoQ supplements, though the evidence for benefit is lacking.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Carnitine shuttles fatty acids into mitochondria but is not implicated in statin myalgia here.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Creatine phosphate is an energy buffer and is not the molecule the brick ties to statin myalgia.
whyWrongByChoice.D: NADPH is a reductant used in cholesterol synthesis, not the muscle molecule linked to statin aches.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Thiamine deficiency is discussed with alcoholism and CNS energy failure, not statin muscle pain.

questions.topicName: Lipids and Lipid Metabolism: Cholesterol Synthesis and Ketone Bodies

questions.stem: A physiology student is asked which circulating hormone is directly synthesized from cholesterol as its precursor. Which of the following is the best answer?

explanation.summary: Steroid hormones such as testosterone are synthesized from cholesterol.
explanation.whyCorrect: Cholesterol is the precursor of all steroid hormones, including the sex hormones estrogen and testosterone, mineralocorticoids like aldosterone, and glucocorticoids like cortisol. Testosterone is a steroid sex hormone and thus requires cholesterol.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Epinephrine is a catecholamine derived from tyrosine, not from cholesterol.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Glucagon is a peptide hormone secreted by the pancreas, not a cholesterol derivative.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Insulin is a peptide hormone from pancreatic beta cells and is not built from cholesterol.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Thyroid hormone is derived from tyrosine and iodine and is not cholesterol-based.

questions.topicName: Lipids and Lipid Metabolism: Cholesterol Synthesis and Ketone Bodies

questions.stem: A 34-year-old man is noted on eye exam to have yellowish plaques on his eyelids and a faint ring around the periphery of his cornea. He also has firm nodular thickening over the Achilles tendon. Given his young age, these findings should most prompt evaluation for which of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A benign, expected consequence of normal aging

explanation.summary: Xanthelasma, corneal arcus, and tendon xanthomas in a young patient suggest an underlying lipid disorder.
explanation.whyCorrect: Xanthomas are lipid-filled foam-cell lesions associated with high cholesterol and metabolic disorders, commonly appearing on tendons of the hands or Achilles. Xanthelasma affects the eyelids and corneal arcus rings the cornea; while these can be benign signs of aging, their appearance in someone younger than 50 is indicative of a lipid disorder.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Corneal arcus and xanthelasma can be benign aging changes, but in a patient under 50 they point to a lipid disorder rather than normal aging.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The lesions reflect lipid accumulation, not primary autoimmune thyroid disease.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Tendon xanthomas are chronic lipid deposits, not an acute bacterial tendon infection.
whyWrongByChoice.E: These cholesterol-laden lesions are not caused by ultraviolet light exposure.

questions.topicName: Lipids and Lipid Metabolism: Cholesterol Synthesis and Ketone Bodies

questions.stem: During prolonged fasting, hepatocytes synthesize ketone bodies from accumulating acetyl-CoA. In which subcellular location does ketone body synthesis occur, contrasting with cholesterol synthesis?

explanation.summary: Ketone bodies are produced in the mitochondrial matrix of the liver, whereas cholesterol synthesis is cytoplasmic.
explanation.whyCorrect: Although both pathways pass through an HMG-CoA intermediate and require three acetyl-CoA, ketone body formation occurs within the mitochondrial matrix while cholesterol synthesis is localized to the cytoplasm. This compartmental separation lets the two pathways use the same intermediate for different purposes.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The cytoplasm is where cholesterol synthesis occurs, not ketone body synthesis.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The Golgi apparatus processes and packages proteins and is not involved in ketogenesis.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Peroxisomes contribute to very-long-chain fatty acid oxidation but are not the site of ketone body synthesis here.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The smooth endoplasmic reticulum is not the site described for ketogenesis.

questions.topicName: Lipids and Lipid Metabolism: Cholesterol Synthesis and Ketone Bodies

questions.stem: During starvation, skeletal muscle takes up circulating ketone bodies and catabolizes them for energy. Catabolism of ketone bodies in these tissues directly regenerates which molecule that then enters the TCA cycle?

explanation.summary: Peripheral tissues convert ketone bodies back into acetyl-CoA to feed the TCA cycle.
explanation.whyCorrect: Ketone bodies are transported without carriers to tissues such as skeletal muscle, cardiac muscle, and renal cortex, which express enzymes that convert them back to acetyl-CoA to supply the TCA cycle. Acetyl-CoA cannot directly give rise to pyruvate or glucose.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Alanine is a gluconeogenic amino acid and is not the product of ketone body catabolism.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Free fatty acid oxidation generates the acetyl-CoA that is packaged into ketone bodies; ketolysis regenerates acetyl-CoA, not fatty acids.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Glucose is not produced from ketone body catabolism; acetyl-CoA cannot yield net glucose.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Pyruvate is a gluconeogenic element; acetyl-CoA from ketolysis cannot be converted directly to pyruvate.

questions.topicName: Lipids and Lipid Metabolism: Cholesterol Synthesis and Ketone Bodies

questions.stem: The liver synthesizes ketone bodies but does not consume them, avoiding a futile cycle of production and catabolism within the same cells. Nominal hepatic expression of which enzyme accounts for the liver's inability to catabolize ketone bodies?

explanation.summary: The liver expresses only nominal beta-ketoacyl-CoA transferase, so it cannot use the ketone bodies it makes.
explanation.whyCorrect: Utilization of ketone bodies requires beta-ketoacyl-CoA transferase, which converts acetoacetate to acetoacetyl-CoA and circumvents the irreversible synthesis steps. Because the liver expresses this enzyme only nominally, it produces ketone bodies but cannot catabolize them, preventing a futile cycle.

whyWrongByChoice.A: beta-hydroxybutyrate dehydrogenase is expressed in the liver and tissues to interconvert acetoacetate and beta-hydroxybutyrate based on NADH.
whyWrongByChoice.C: HMG-CoA reductase catalyzes the rate-limiting step of cholesterol synthesis, not ketone catabolism.
whyWrongByChoice.D: HMG-CoA synthase is actually a liver ketogenic enzyme, not the one absent from the liver.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Thiolase is present in the liver as the last step of beta-oxidation and the first step of ketone synthesis.

questions.topicName: Lipids and Lipid Metabolism: Cholesterol Synthesis and Ketone Bodies

questions.stem: A 30-year-old woman presents with rapid weight loss after several weeks on a strict high-fat, low-carbohydrate diet. Blood pressure is 112/74 mmHg and heart rate is 90/min. Exam shows reduced muscle mass and adipose tissue. Urine shows elevated ketones but no glucose or reducing sugars. Which metabolic adaptation primarily contributes to her ketosis?

explanation.summary: In dietary ketosis, glucagon-driven fatty acid oxidation floods the liver with acetyl-CoA, producing ketone bodies.
explanation.whyCorrect: Her low insulin/glucagon ratio mobilizes triglyceride stores from adipocytes to fuel hepatic gluconeogenesis. Fatty acid oxidation produces acetyl-CoA for the TCA to power gluconeogenesis, and the combination of rising acetyl-CoA and the pulling of oxaloacetate into gluconeogenesis leads to acetyl-CoA accumulation and ketone body production.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Chylomicron formation follows a high-fat meal and delivers carbons for use, but it is not the adaptation driving her ketosis.
whyWrongByChoice.B: There is no evidence of pathologic insulin-signaling disruption in this healthy dieter; her hormonal state is a normal low insulin/glucagon ratio.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Glycolysis would not be heightened when dietary glucose is limited.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Lipogenesis is an anabolic process, but she is in a catabolic, fat-mobilizing state.

questions.topicName: Lipids and Lipid Metabolism: Cholesterol Synthesis and Ketone Bodies

questions.stem: A 24-year-old man with a history of alcohol abuse reports drinking large amounts of whiskey over several days. Blood pressure is 100/60 mmHg and respiratory rate is 18/min. Labs show elevated lactate, a high anion gap metabolic acidosis, hypoglycemia, and elevated serum ketones. Which parameter is most directly contributing to his ketone body production?

explanation.summary: Alcohol metabolism raises the hepatic NADH/NAD+ ratio, which slows the TCA and gluconeogenesis and drives ketogenesis.
explanation.whyCorrect: Alcohol metabolism increases the NADH/NAD+ ratio, favoring conversion of pyruvate to lactate (depriving gluconeogenesis of substrate) and oxaloacetate to malate. This depletes and slows the TCA cycle, so acetyl-CoA accumulates and is shunted into ketone body synthesis, producing hypoglycemia and ketoacidosis.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Pyruvate is actually diverted to lactate and reduced, not increased, in this high-NADH state.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The metabolic acidosis is a result of the accumulating ketones and lactate, not the cause of ketone production.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Decreased, not sustained, insulin signaling favors ketone body formation.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Thiamine deficiency is associated with alcoholism and hypoglycemia management but does not directly cause ketone body formation.

questions.topicName: Lipids and Lipid Metabolism: Cholesterol Synthesis and Ketone Bodies

questions.stem: A 19-year-old with newly diagnosed type 1 diabetes presents in diabetic ketoacidosis. Despite a very high plasma glucose, his tissues behave as if starving. Which underlying abnormality best explains why his body remains in a catabolic, ketone-producing state?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A primary deficiency of glucagon secretion

choices.label: B
choices.text: Excess insulin driving glucose into all tissues

choices.label: C
choices.text: Inability to absorb dietary carbohydrate from the gut

choices.label: D
choices.text: Insulin insufficiency preventing glucose uptake via GLUT4

explanation.summary: In DKA, insulin insufficiency prevents insulin-dependent glucose uptake, so tissues sense starvation despite high glucose.
explanation.whyCorrect: The fundamental cause of DKA is insulin insufficiency, most common in type 1 diabetics who cannot synthesize insulin. Insulin is required for tissues like skeletal muscle and adipocytes to take up glucose via GLUT4, so in its absence the body perceives a starving state despite abundant plasma glucose, promoting fatty acid liberation, gluconeogenesis, and ketone body production.

whyWrongByChoice.A: DKA arises from insulin deficiency; glucagon signaling is relatively unopposed rather than deficient.
whyWrongByChoice.B: DKA reflects a lack of insulin, not an excess driving glucose into tissues.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The problem is cellular glucose uptake due to missing insulin, not intestinal carbohydrate absorption.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Loss of glucose-6-phosphatase would impair glucose release, not explain the insulin-deficient starvation state of DKA.

questions.topicName: Lipids and Lipid Metabolism: Cholesterol Synthesis and Ketone Bodies

questions.stem: A patient in severe diabetic ketoacidosis exhibits labored, rapid, deep breathing. This respiratory pattern is a compensatory response to the acid load. What is the physiologic purpose of this breathing pattern?

choices.label: A
choices.text: To exhale CO2 and shift the bicarbonate buffer to consume excess protons

choices.label: B
choices.text: To exhale volatile ketone bodies directly from the alveolar surface

choices.label: C
choices.text: To increase oxygen delivery and thereby correct the underlying hypoglycemia

choices.label: D
choices.text: To increase renal bicarbonate reabsorption in the proximal tubule

choices.label: E
choices.text: To retain CO2 and raise the blood carbonic acid concentration

explanation.summary: Kussmaul respirations blow off CO2, driving the bicarbonate buffer toward consuming excess protons to relieve acidosis.
explanation.whyCorrect: Accumulating ketone bodies act as metabolic acids and cause a high anion gap metabolic acidosis. Labored deep breathing (Kussmaul respirations) rapidly exhales CO2, shifting the bicarbonate buffering equilibrium (HCO3- + H+ to H2CO3 to CO2 + H2O) so that excess protons are consumed, helping relieve the drop in pH.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Fruity breath comes from volatile acetone, but Kussmaul breathing itself functions to blow off CO2, not to exhale ketone acids as a compensation.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The breathing pattern compensates for acidosis and does not correct the hypoglycemia.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Kussmaul respirations are a pulmonary, not renal, compensatory mechanism for the acid load.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Retaining CO2 and raising carbonic acid would worsen the acidosis, the opposite of the compensatory goal.

questions.topicName: Lipids and Lipid Metabolism: Cholesterol Synthesis and Ketone Bodies

questions.stem: A biochemist quantifies endogenous cholesterol production across tissues in a healthy adult. Although every tissue type in the body contains cells capable of synthesizing cholesterol, two organs together account for roughly 80% of the body's need. Which pair of organs is it?

explanation.summary: The liver and intestine are the major cholesterol producers, together supplying about 80% of the body's need.
explanation.whyCorrect: Cholesterol is an essential membrane component and precursor for steroid hormones, bile acids, and vitamin D. Though every tissue type has cells that can make cholesterol, the liver and intestine are the major producers, together accounting for about 80% of the body's requirement via the endogenous synthetic pathway.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Adipose tissue and skeletal muscle store and burn fuel but are not the major cholesterol-producing organs.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Brain and skin can make cholesterol like all tissues but do not account for the bulk of endogenous production.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The kidney and adrenal cortex use cholesterol (e.g. for aldosterone and cortisol) but are not the major producers of it.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The pancreas and spleen are not identified as major sites of cholesterol synthesis.

questions.topicName: Lipids and Lipid Metabolism: Cholesterol Synthesis and Ketone Bodies

questions.stem: In a cell-free extract of hepatocyte cytoplasm, HMG-CoA is converted to mevalonate only when a specific reduced cofactor is supplied. Which cofactor is consumed by HMG-CoA reductase in this reaction?

explanation.summary: HMG-CoA reductase reduces HMG-CoA to mevalonate using NADPH, generating NADP+.
explanation.whyCorrect: Synthesis reactions reduce carbon substrates to build larger macromolecules, whereas catabolic processes oxidize them. The rate-limiting reduction of HMG-CoA into mevalonate by HMG-CoA reductase consumes NADPH and releases NADP+, as shown in the cholesterol synthesis pathway.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Biotin is a carboxylase cofactor (e.g. pyruvate carboxylase) and plays no role in HMG-CoA reduction.
whyWrongByChoice.B: FADH2 is generated during oxidative catabolism and is not the reductant for mevalonate formation.
whyWrongByChoice.C: NADH is the reductant used by 3-hydroxybutyrate dehydrogenase in the mitochondrial matrix, not by cytoplasmic HMG-CoA reductase.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Thiamin is emphasized for CNS glucose utilization in alcoholics, not for cholesterol synthesis.

questions.topicName: Lipids and Lipid Metabolism: Cholesterol Synthesis and Ketone Bodies

questions.stem: A research group measures hepatic HMG-CoA reductase activity every 4 hours over a full day in healthy volunteers who eat three regular meals. At which time is enzyme activity expected to peak?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Activity remains constant across the 24 hours

choices.label: B
choices.text: During the night, while the volunteers are fasting

choices.label: D
choices.text: In the mid-afternoon, after the largest meal

choices.label: E
choices.text: Within the first hour after breakfast

explanation.summary: HMG-CoA reductase activity follows a circadian rhythm and peaks at night when the body is fasting.
explanation.whyCorrect: One of the factors governing HMG-CoA reductase is diurnal variation: the enzyme's activity follows a circadian rhythm, peaking during the night when the body is fasting. This is why activity measured in a 24-hour profile is highest overnight rather than after meals.

whyWrongByChoice.A: HMG-CoA reductase activity is not constant; it shows a defined circadian rhythm.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Exercise timing is not described as a driver of HMG-CoA reductase activity; the peak is nocturnal.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Activity does not peak in the afternoon following the largest meal; the circadian peak is at night.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The peak is tied to the nocturnal fasting period, not to the immediate post-breakfast window.

questions.topicName: Lipids and Lipid Metabolism: Cholesterol Synthesis and Ketone Bodies

questions.stem: A 40-year-old woman changes her eating pattern for several weeks. Which of the following dietary patterns would be expected to increase the activity of her hepatic HMG-CoA reductase?

choices.label: A
choices.text: High in cholesterol, high in fat

choices.label: B
choices.text: High in cholesterol, low in carbohydrate

choices.label: C
choices.text: High in fat, low in carbohydrate

choices.label: D
choices.text: High in protein, low in carbohydrate

choices.label: E
choices.text: Low in cholesterol, high in carbohydrate

explanation.summary: A low-cholesterol diet or a diet high in carbohydrate content increases HMG-CoA reductase activity.
explanation.whyCorrect: Diet is one of several factors that increase HMG-CoA reductase activity: a low cholesterol diet or a diet high in carbohydrate content increases the enzyme's activity. Reduced exogenous cholesterol and abundant carbohydrate favor endogenous cholesterol production.

whyWrongByChoice.A: High dietary cholesterol and fat do not increase HMG-CoA reductase activity; low cholesterol intake does.
whyWrongByChoice.B: A cholesterol-rich, low-carbohydrate diet is the opposite of the pattern that increases enzyme activity.
whyWrongByChoice.C: A high-fat, low-carbohydrate diet lacks the high carbohydrate content that increases HMG-CoA reductase activity.
whyWrongByChoice.D: A high-protein, low-carbohydrate diet does not supply the carbohydrate load that upregulates the enzyme.

questions.topicName: Lipids and Lipid Metabolism: Cholesterol Synthesis and Ketone Bodies

questions.stem: A physiologist studies the hormonal governance of hepatic cholesterol synthesis. Which pair of hormones positively influences HMG-CoA reductase activity?

explanation.summary: Both insulin and thyroid hormones positively influence HMG-CoA reductase activity.
explanation.whyCorrect: Hormonal governance is one of the factors that increase HMG-CoA reductase activity: both insulin and thyroid hormones positively influence the enzyme. This fits the fed, anabolic state in which synthesis reactions predominate.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Cortisol and aldosterone are steroid products made from cholesterol, not the hormones that positively regulate its synthesis.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Thyroid hormone is correct, but epinephrine promotes catabolic fatty acid oxidation rather than HMG-CoA reductase activity.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Glucagon is the fasting hormone that mobilizes fatty acids for ketogenesis; it is not the hormone described as increasing HMG-CoA reductase activity.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Glucagon and the catecholamine epinephrine drive triglyceride breakdown and fatty acid oxidation, not cholesterol synthesis.

questions.topicName: Lipids and Lipid Metabolism: Cholesterol Synthesis and Ketone Bodies

questions.stem: A 61-year-old man has been taking a statin for 4 months for hypercholesterolemia. At a follow-up visit he feels well. Which of the following laboratory values is most likely to be elevated as a recognized effect of this drug class?

explanation.summary: Statins can raise liver biomarkers such as ALT and AST.
explanation.whyCorrect: Beyond lowering serum cholesterol and reducing atherosclerotic plaque formation, statins can raise liver biomarkers (e.g. ALT and AST). Along with muscle pain, this is one of the recognized side effects to monitor in patients on statin therapy.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Amylase reflects pancreatic injury and is not the biomarker statins are known to elevate.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Creatinine reflects renal function and is not the biomarker described as rising with statins.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Serum potassium is not a described statin effect.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Thyroid-stimulating hormone is not affected by statin therapy; thyroid hormone is a regulator of HMG-CoA reductase, not a statin target.

questions.topicName: Lipids and Lipid Metabolism: Cholesterol Synthesis and Ketone Bodies

questions.stem: A 48-year-old man with poorly controlled diabetes and markedly elevated lipids develops crops of small yellow papules on his skin. The lesions are inflamed, itchy, and tender, and several of them ooze. Which of the following best describes these lesions?

explanation.summary: Eruptive xanthomas are inflamed, oozing, itchy or tender lesions caused by excessive fat accumulation under the skin.
explanation.whyCorrect: Xanthomas are lipid-filled foam-cell lesions associated with diabetes, high cholesterol, liver disease, and metabolic disorders. Eruptive xanthomas specifically become inflamed and ooze due to excessive accumulation of fats under the skin, and they may be itchy, tender, or painful.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Tendon xanthomas are firm nodular deposits on tendons of the hands or Achilles, not inflamed oozing papules.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Corneal arcus is a faint cholesterol ring around the edge of the cornea, not a skin lesion.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Peripheral artery disease from lipid accumulation manifests as reduced blood flow (e.g. absent leg hair), not eruptive skin papules.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Xanthelasma presents as yellowish plaques on or around the eyelids, not inflamed oozing papules.

questions.topicName: Lipids and Lipid Metabolism: Cholesterol Synthesis and Ketone Bodies

questions.stem: A medical student reviews the three classic ketone bodies. Which of the following is excluded as a ketone body by some sources because it is obtained by nonenzymatic decomposition and is not used to produce acetyl-CoA?

explanation.summary: Acetone forms by spontaneous, nonenzymatic decomposition of acetoacetate and is not used to make acetyl-CoA.
explanation.whyCorrect: Some sources exclude acetone as a ketone body because it is obtained by nonenzymatic acetoacetate decomposition and is not used to produce acetyl-CoA. Despite not being used for energy, acetone is clinically relevant: its low vapor pressure allows it to be exhaled from the lungs, producing the fruity breath of patients with high ketone levels.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Acetoacetate is formed enzymatically by HMG-CoA lyase and is the first ketone body catabolized for fuel.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Acetoacetyl-CoA is an intermediate of ketone body synthesis and ketolysis, not a ketone body.
whyWrongByChoice.D: beta-Hydroxybutyrate is formed enzymatically by 3-hydroxybutyrate dehydrogenase and is catabolized for fuel; it is only notable for not being chemically a ketone.
whyWrongByChoice.E: HMG-CoA is the intermediate shared by ketone body and cholesterol synthesis, not a ketone body.

questions.topicName: Lipids and Lipid Metabolism: Cholesterol Synthesis and Ketone Bodies

questions.stem: A 35-year-old man is on the third day of a water-only fast. Hepatic beta-oxidation flux is high, and NADH predominates in the mitochondrial matrix. Which ketone body is preferentially formed under these conditions?

explanation.summary: High matrix NADH during fasting drives 3-hydroxybutyrate dehydrogenase to reduce acetoacetate to 3-hydroxybutyrate.
explanation.whyCorrect: Acetoacetate can be reduced to 3-hydroxybutyrate by 3-hydroxybutyrate dehydrogenase, which consumes NADH. Because NADH predominates in the matrix during fasting due to increased beta-oxidation flux in hepatic mitochondria, formation of 3-hydroxybutyrate is favored.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Acetoacetate is the substrate that is reduced when NADH is abundant, so it is consumed rather than favored.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Acetoacetyl-CoA is an upstream intermediate formed by thiolase, not a circulating ketone body.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Acetone arises from spontaneous degradation of acetoacetate and is not the NADH-favored product.
whyWrongByChoice.E: HMG-CoA is the intermediate cleaved by HMG-CoA lyase, not the ketone body favored by high NADH.

questions.topicName: Lipids and Lipid Metabolism: Cholesterol Synthesis and Ketone Bodies

questions.stem: A 22-year-old woman with diabetic ketoacidosis has a high anion gap metabolic acidosis. Which chemical property of acetoacetate and beta-hydroxybutyrate accounts for their ability to produce this acidosis?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Their carbonyl groups accept protons from carbonic acid

choices.label: B
choices.text: Their carboxyl groups have low pKa values and release protons

choices.label: C
choices.text: Their high vapor pressure causes retention of CO2

choices.label: D
choices.text: They are converted to lactate in peripheral tissues

choices.label: E
choices.text: They block renal excretion of hydrogen ions

explanation.summary: Acetoacetate and beta-hydroxybutyrate carry carboxyl groups with low pKa values, so they release protons and act as acids.
explanation.whyCorrect: Both acetoacetate and beta-hydroxybutyrate contain carboxyl functional groups that have low pKa values, allowing them to release protons and function as acids within the body. Excess accumulation of these metabolic acids leads to a high anion gap metabolic acidosis.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The acidity comes from proton release by carboxyl groups, not from carbonyl groups accepting protons; beta-hydroxybutyrate does not even have a ketone carbonyl.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Low vapor pressure is the property of acetone that allows it to be exhaled; the acidosis is not caused by CO2 retention, which Kussmaul breathing actually reduces.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Ketone bodies are converted back to acetyl-CoA in tissues, not to lactate; lactate rises in alcoholism from pyruvate shunting.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The acidosis results from proton release by the ketone bodies themselves, not from blocked renal acid excretion.

questions.topicName: Lipids and Lipid Metabolism: Cholesterol Synthesis and Ketone Bodies

questions.stem: A healthy 28-year-old wakes after 8 hours of sleep without having eaten overnight. Constant low-level ketone body production has occurred during this short fast. Which tissues primarily catabolize the ketone bodies produced under these conditions?

explanation.summary: Ketone bodies made during a short overnight fast are largely catabolized by skeletal and cardiac muscle, sparing glucose for the brain and RBCs.
explanation.whyCorrect: Constant low-level ketone body production occurs with a short overnight fast as we sleep. Ketone bodies synthesized under these conditions are largely catabolized by tissues such as skeletal and cardiac muscle. Their utilization reduces reliance upon glucose, sparing it for the brain and RBCs.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Red blood cells lack mitochondria and cannot consume ketone bodies; they exclusively use glucose.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The brain only promotes ketone body utilization after prolonged glucose deprivation (~2-4 days), not during an overnight fast.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The liver synthesizes ketone bodies but does not consume them, and the intestine is not described as a ketone consumer.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Adipose tissue supplies the free fatty acids that fuel ketogenesis; it is not the tissue that catabolizes ketone bodies.

questions.topicName: Lipids and Lipid Metabolism: Cholesterol Synthesis and Ketone Bodies

questions.stem: A 30-year-old man begins a complete fast. Approximately when does hepatic ketone body formation increase dramatically and enzymatic expression in the brain begin to promote ketone body utilization in lieu of glucose?

choices.label: A
choices.text: After about 2-4 days, once glycogen stores are depleted

choices.label: B
choices.text: After about 3-4 weeks, once muscle protein is exhausted

choices.label: C
choices.text: After one overnight fast, when glycogenolysis peaks

choices.label: D
choices.text: Only after refeeding, when insulin secretion rises

choices.label: E
choices.text: Within the first 6 hours, before glycogenolysis starts

explanation.summary: Ketone body formation rises dramatically after ~2-4 days of glucose deprivation, when glycogen is depleted and gluconeogenesis is heavily stimulated.
explanation.whyCorrect: The formation of ketone bodies increases dramatically during prolonged periods of glucose deprivation, approximately 2-4 days in, when all glycogen stores are depleted and gluconeogenesis is heavily stimulated. At this point enzymatic expression in the brain promotes ketone body utilization in lieu of glucose, sparing glucose for RBCs.

whyWrongByChoice.B: The switch occurs at the 2-4 day mark when glycogen is depleted, well before weeks of fasting.
whyWrongByChoice.C: After an overnight fast ketone production is low-level and consumed by muscle; the brain has not yet switched.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Refeeding and rising insulin shut ketone production off nearly immediately rather than triggering it.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Only constant low-level ketone production occurs early in a fast; the dramatic rise and brain adaptation require days, not hours.

questions.topicName: Lipids and Lipid Metabolism: Cholesterol Synthesis and Ketone Bodies

questions.stem: During the second week of starvation, most tissues have shifted toward fatty acids or ketone bodies for ATP production. Which of the following cell types remains exclusively dependent on glucose for ATP production?

explanation.summary: RBCs lack mitochondria, so they cannot use fatty acids or ketone bodies and rely exclusively on glucose.
explanation.whyCorrect: RBCs are unable to convert fatty acids to ATP because they lack mitochondria, and for the same reason they are also unable to consume ketone bodies. They exclusively use glucose for ATP production, which is why the shift of other organs to ketone bodies is a glucose-sparing mechanism that protects the RBC fuel supply.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Cardiac muscle catabolizes fatty acids and readily converts ketone bodies to ATP.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The brain prefers glucose but adapts to derive acetyl-CoA from ketone bodies during prolonged fasting.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The renal cortex is one of the select organs that converts ketone bodies back to acetyl-CoA for the TCA cycle.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Skeletal muscle catabolizes fatty acids for ATP and consumes ketone bodies even during a short overnight fast.

questions.topicName: Lipids and Lipid Metabolism: Cholesterol Synthesis and Ketone Bodies

questions.stem: A 45-year-old woman is on the fifth day of a prolonged fast. Which of the following best characterizes her brain's fuel utilization at this time?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It obtains acetyl-CoA from ketone bodies, not free fatty acids

choices.label: B
choices.text: It oxidizes free fatty acids released from adipose tissue

choices.label: C
choices.text: It relies on its own glycogen stores until refeeding

choices.label: D
choices.text: It shifts entirely to lactate produced by muscle

choices.label: E
choices.text: It takes up triglycerides from circulating lipoproteins

explanation.summary: In prolonged glucose deprivation the brain induces enzymes to derive acetyl-CoA from ketone bodies, but it cannot use free fatty acids.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brain prefers glucose and constitutes ~65% of the body's glucose requirements. In prolonged glucose deprivation it induces enzymes that allow acetyl-CoA to be derived from ketone bodies; however, the brain is unable to use free fatty acids during this same time. It therefore becomes highly reliant on ketone bodies to spare glucose from hepatic gluconeogenesis for RBCs.

whyWrongByChoice.B: The brain is unable to use free fatty acids, which is precisely why it must rely on ketone bodies.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The brain's adaptation is to circulating ketone bodies, not to an internal glycogen reserve.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Lactate accumulation is described in alcoholism from NADH-driven pyruvate shunting, not as the brain's fasting fuel.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The brain does not take up triglycerides from lipoproteins as its fasting fuel; ketone bodies are the fat-derived fuel it can use.

questions.topicName: Lipids and Lipid Metabolism: Cholesterol Synthesis and Ketone Bodies

questions.stem: A 38-year-old man who has fasted for 6 days eats a large carbohydrate-rich meal. Which of the following best describes the metabolic response over the next several hours?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Hepatic ketogenesis persists until its enzymes are degraded

choices.label: B
choices.text: Red blood cells begin to consume ketone bodies

choices.label: C
choices.text: The brain abruptly resumes glucose use and ketogenesis ceases

choices.label: D
choices.text: The brain remains ketone-dependent for several more days

choices.label: E
choices.text: The liver begins to catabolize circulating ketone bodies

explanation.summary: The brain always prefers glucose and switches back abruptly on refeeding, while hepatic ketone production stops nearly immediately.
explanation.whyCorrect: While it may take several days for the brain to adapt to utilize ketone bodies, the brain always prefers glucose.
